research_mode: official primary sources only; police open-data, ONS crime methodology and Home Office outcome-methodology gates; no parcel result, local risk score or business result claimed

sources.name: Two-source crime framework
verified_claims: Crime in England and Wales primarily uses the Crime Survey for England and Wales and police recorded crime.
limitations: Neither source alone is a complete count of crime and their scopes must not be conflated.

sources.name: CSEW collection design
verified_claims: The CSEW is a face-to-face survey of around 31,000 people aged 16 or over in England and Wales.
limitations: Survey estimates are not a census and cannot support exact local incident counts.

sources.name: Crime statistics publication frequency
verified_claims: Crime in England and Wales statistics are produced quarterly from survey and administrative data.
limitations: Quarterly publication does not mean all underlying records have the same reference period or revision status.

sources.name: CSEW reference period
verified_claims: CSEW respondents report experiences of crime in the 12 months before interview.
limitations: Recall over a 12-month period can introduce telescoping, omission and other non-sampling error.

sources.name: CSEW population and offence exclusions
verified_claims: The main CSEW estimates exclude crimes against businesses, people not resident in households, homicide and victimless crimes such as drug possession.
limitations: CSEW figures must not be presented as covering those excluded populations or offences.

sources.name: CSEW provisional response rate
verified_claims: The provisional CSEW response rate for the year ending March 2026 was 48%, and ONS reported that its quality review found little impact on estimate reliability.
limitations: The lower response rate still requires uncertainty and non-response limitations to be retained.

sources.name: Police recorded crime force coverage
verified_claims: Police recorded crime figures are supplied through the Home Office by 43 territorial forces and British Transport Police.
limitations: Force coverage does not guarantee uniform recording practice, completeness or timeliness.

sources.name: Notifiable-offence scope
verified_claims: Police recorded crime coverage is defined by the Notifiable Offence List and excludes non-notifiable matters such as anti-social behaviour and parking offences.
limitations: Recorded-crime totals must not be interpreted as all incidents dealt with by police.

sources.name: Combined-source completeness boundary
verified_claims: CSEW and police recorded crime together provide a broader picture, but neither provides a complete count and both have exclusions.
limitations: Combining the sources must not involve adding non-comparable counts or eliminating their separate limitations.

sources.name: CSEW long-term trend strength
verified_claims: ONS describes CSEW as the most reliable indicator for long-term trends in common crimes because it includes unreported crime and is unaffected by police activity and recording changes.
limitations: This strength does not make CSEW suitable for low-volume, excluded or highly local crime estimates.

sources.name: CSEW sampling error
verified_claims: CSEW estimates are subject to sampling error because they are based on a sample rather than a census.
limitations: Point estimates must retain confidence intervals and should not be treated as precise counts.

sources.name: CSEW non-sampling error
verified_claims: CSEW estimates can be affected by recall, non-disclosure, socially desirable responses and interviewer or coding error.
limitations: These errors cannot be removed merely by increasing displayed decimal precision.

sources.name: Low-volume crime variability
verified_claims: The CSEW sample produces substantial variability for less frequent crime types, making short-term trends difficult to detect.
limitations: Small changes in low-volume estimates must not be promoted as meaningful without uncertainty testing.

sources.name: Well-recorded police crime use
verified_claims: For offences that are well reported and accurately recorded, police data can provide a useful picture of volume.
limitations: The condition must be assessed by offence and period rather than assumed for all police-recorded crime.

sources.name: Police demand interpretation
verified_claims: Police recorded crime provides insight into demands placed on police and where policing effort is spent.
limitations: Demand on police is not equivalent to the prevalence of crime in the population.

sources.name: Police-recorded trend limitation
verified_claims: For many offences, police recorded crime is affected by reporting behaviour, police activity and recording practice and is not a reliable measure of underlying levels or trends.
limitations: A local increase may reflect recording or reporting changes and must not automatically be labelled increased risk.

sources.name: Police-recorded accreditation status
verified_claims: Police recorded crime statistics do not currently meet the required standard for designation as accredited official statistics.
limitations: Official publication status must not be represented as accredited status.

sources.name: CSEW unreported-crime coverage
verified_claims: The CSEW includes crimes not reported to or recorded by police and acts as an independent check on police figures.
limitations: Survey coverage does not identify individual unreported incidents or their exact locations.

sources.name: International comparability boundary
verified_claims: International crime comparisons are difficult because legal systems, definitions, surveys and recording practices differ.
limitations: England and Wales figures must not be directly ranked against other countries without methodological harmonisation.

sources.name: Police-force-area sample target
verified_claims: The CSEW sample design targets at least 585 interviews in each police force area.
limitations: The target supports area estimates but does not justify neighbourhood, LSOA or parcel-level inference.
